claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi matrix is homogeneous and single-phase.
A controlled thermomechanical or annealing treatment can induce nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates in CoCrFeNi.
Nanoprecipitates coupled with the primary grain structure form a nanohierarchical architecture.
Nano-coupled grains and dispersed nanoprecipitates create a graded microstructure.
The nanohierarchical structure releases frictional stress in stages during room-temperature wear.
At low temperatures, nanoscale heterogeneity provides multiple deformation and energy-dissipation pathways.
These low-temperature deformation pathways lower the coefficient of friction.
At 800 °C, the nanohierarchical structure promotes a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer.
The dense nanocrystalline glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear at 800 °C.
The treated CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The treated CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower wear rate than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Untreated CoCrFeNi typically exhibits increased friction and wear, especially at elevated temperatures.
The elevated-temperature tribological degradation of untreated CoCrFeNi is caused by its lack of adaptive microstructural features.
The proposed performance applies under approximately 5 N reciprocating sliding at about 1 Hz.
The proposed performance applies in ambient air from room temperature through 800 °C.
Prior evidence shows wear rates on the order of 10^-7 to 10^-6 mm3/Nm from room temperature to 800 °C for a nanohierarchical Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 alloy.
The optimal nanoprecipitate volume fraction, size distribution, and processing parameters for CoCrFeNi have not been determined.
